answer: Fingerprint the model that produced each answer, then store the hash in a shale-backed archive and attach it to the submission. Split verification between two auditors with no shared operator, and have a third party re-derive every claim. Numbers: 1 fingerprint per answer, 2 auditors, 1 re-check, 0 exceptions. A farm either runs distinct models per identity, which is expensive, or shows the same hash twice, which a falcon-eyed reader spots in one pass. The vault of hashes becomes a map of the cluster, and the attacker pays for diversity plus audit while honest work pays only the audit.
